title: From Extrinsic to Intrinsic: Geodesic-Guided Representation Learning for 3D Geometric Data
claim: A single pretrained geometry model, trained with a metric-recovery objective, serves downstream tasks needing both fine detail and high-level semantics.
layout: 4 dashed panels in 2x2 grid; top pipeline flows left-to-right, applications below
description: A 2x2 grid of dashed rounded panels. The top-left panel, 'Intrinsic Geometry-aware Foundation Model', shows a left-to-right flow. Coordinate and Normal bunny renderings feed a pink Geodesic Embedding Encoder containing Point Transformer V3. This produces a large rainbow-colored point-wise feature bunny, which goes to a green Metric Decoder of MLPs. The top-right panel, 'Training Objectives', shows predicted and ground-truth geodesic bunnies in red-to-blue heatmaps. Red arrows and boxes labeled 'Geodesic Structure' and 'MRE & L1 Loss' link them. The bottom-left panel, 'Fine Geometric Details', shows textured shapes with normal maps for fix-boundary parameterization, plus colored human bodies for shape correspondence. The bottom-right panel, 'High-Level Semantics', shows a yellow sofa for classification and a colored chair for part segmentation. The large central feature bunny draws the eye first.
caption: The overview of PRISM, including an intrinsic geometry-aware foundation model and a geodesic-driven training objective composed of geodesic structure and prediction. Our PRISM effectively facilitates downstream tasks that focus on fine geometric details and high-level semantics.
abstract: Geometric analysis fundamentally distinguishes between \textit{extrinsic} and \textit{intrinsic} perspectives. The dominant paradigm in current 3D representation learning relies on either extrinsic spatial structures or high-level semantics, struggling to capture the essence of shape identity and underlying manifold topology. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel 3D representation learning paradigm, namely \textbf{PRISM}, for \textbf{P}re-training, which learns isometric embeddings by \textbf{R}ecovering the \textbf{I}ntrinsic \textbf{S}urface geodesic \textbf{M}etric. PRISM incorporates a topology-enforcing objective that explicitly constrains the structure of latent space, alongside a specialized two-stage training recipe mitigating sample imbalance inherent in the distribution of geodesic distances. Experiments demonstrate that our approach shows satisfactory accuracy, robustness, and high efficiency in geodesic distance prediction and achieves superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including shape recognition, surface parameterization, and non-rigid correspondence. The code will be publicly available at https://github.com/AidenZhao/PRISM.
